data.did_you_know: This artist devoted his work to depicting Inuit traditions that were fast disappearing in the Arctic.
data.description:
Alec (Peter) Aliknak Banksland made this print using stonecut, a technique developed by Inuit peoples in the Arctic. It involves drawing on a prepared stone and cutting away the areas that should not be printed before rolling ink and
pressing a sheet of paper on its surface. The artist used the process—which creates a single unique print—for depictions of Inuit traditions at a time when tribe members were being forced into settlements by the Canadian government.
